arena: Classic Generic procedural_v2 11x9, two players, 2400-action horizon
method: Against the identical frozen routed-v6 direct opponent on every map and rotated seat, select exact native three-turn search or frozen routed-v6 direct once at each candidate-seat turn start by a deterministic seed/seat/turn hash. The selected policy controls that whole turn. Run the predeclared 0%,25%,50%,75%,100% teacher-turn arms on the same maps; keep all policies frozen.
interpretation: Even roughly one quarter of exact three-turn teacher-controlled whole turns improved this fixed-pool outcome on fresh maps, with both seats gaining. In this setting, benefit does not require near-total exact search coverage. This does not establish why an earlier behavioral-cloning student trained on a different two-turn teacher failed. The 50% and 75% arms are not monotonic in this finite sample. A trained student is not a deterministic mixture of exact teacher turns: it may introduce wrong actions even where source and teacher agree, select different states, or fail to complete teacher plans. The earlier held-out two-turn BC audit found 255 exact teacher corrections among 870 source/teacher disagreements, 193 actions matching neither, and 124 new deviations where source already matched teacher; that specific student also had higher whole-turn teacher fidelity yet weaker complete-game results. These observations motivate measuring correction precision and harmful novel errors, not merely teacher-action accuracy or another isolated-terminal label. The four descriptive map tests share a baseline and are not independent promotion gates.

verification.resource_policy: SSH server fedora-toolbox, pinned single CPU, nice19, no GPU

decision: This mixture is a diagnostic, not a neural student, Elo rating or playable candidate. Keep all policies unchanged. Next audit existing student mistakes against source and teacher at identical states with outcome-aware grouping, then predeclare disjoint training and complete-game validation before any new distillation approach.
